hero.angle: Fort Pierce's entire legal team resigning after the city attorney's contract was not renewed, leaving the city without counsel and forcing a $31,000 outside search — with commissioners divided over motive and impact on pending development.

hero.body:
Fort Pierce's city commission held a heated special meeting Monday after nearly the city's entire legal team resigned, leaving the city with no attorneys and forcing officials to spend $31,000 in taxpayer money to find a permanent replacement. The mass departure followed the city's decision not to renew the current city attorney's contract, which expires in September. City staff confirmed that aside from one paralegal, the entire legal department has left.

City Commissioner Michael Broderick told WPTV the situation is a self-inflicted wound. He said he is not aware of any complaints, disciplinary action or poor performance reviews that would lead to the city attorney leaving. Broderick said the departures included at least three city attorneys. Commissioner Chris Dzadovsky suggested the resignations were orchestrated, though he did not say who he believed orchestrated the mass resignation.

Broderick expressed concern that the lack of legal representation could make it easier for developers to push projects through, particularly on South Hutchinson Island, where a 900-unit residential project is already pending at Causeway Cove. Dzadovsky disagreed, arguing the absence of legal staff would actually slow development down because it would take longer to have city attorney legal review.

The commission approved the $31,000 contract for an outside search firm despite sharp criticism from Broderick and taxpayer Kevin Keene during public comment. City Human Resources Manager Jared Sorenson defended the decision, saying an outside firm was needed to keep the process impartial. The commission appointed Deputy City Manager Camille Wallace as interim city attorney while the permanent search is conducted.

hero.angle: Lead with the manslaughter charge against Jabari Cowart following the fatal BB gun shooting on Avenue G, detailing how the informal gathering turned deadly and the victim's death at Lawnwood Hospital.

hero.body:
A Fort Pierce man faces a manslaughter charge after a 34-year-old man died following a BB gun shooting on August 22, 2026, in the 2900 block of Avenue G. Fort Pierce Police officers responded to reports of a gunshot victim and found the 34-year-old male suffering from an injury. He was transported to Lawnwood Hospital, where he later died.

The investigation revealed that a group of males had been shooting a BB gun at trees when the suspect, Jabari Cowart, 36, asked to use the BB gun. During the interaction, Cowart pointed the BB gun in the victim's direction and fired. Shortly thereafter, the victim collapsed.

Cowart was charged with manslaughter and taken to the St. Lucie County Jail. The circumstances surrounding the incident remain under investigation by Fort Pierce Police.

The shooting occurred Saturday, and the charges were filed as investigators determined the victim's death resulted from the BB gun incident. Police have not released the name of the victim.

hero.angle: Comprehensive wrap of Sunday's confirmed EF0 tornado/waterspout in Port St. Lucie — NWS damage survey findings combined with resident accounts of fences, sheds and pool enclosures destroyed near Southbend, plus reports of related storm damage in Jensen Beach, to give readers the fullest single account of the event and cleanup underway.

hero.body:
The National Weather Service confirmed an EF0 tornado with peak winds of 75 mph touched down in Port St. Lucie Sunday evening, damaging 20 to 30 homes along a 2.1-mile path. Will Ulrich, warning coordination meteorologist with the National Weather Service Melbourne office, announced the findings Monday morning during a press conference at Jessica Clinton Park following a damage survey of the affected areas.

The tornado, classified as a landspout, first touched down at 6:10 p.m. near Southeast Kitching Cove Lane and Southeast Morningside Boulevard, close to the Tarpon Bay Yacht Club. It produced minimal structural damage, including roof damage, soffit damage and pool enclosures lifted from their foundations. The tornado then moved over the St. Lucie River, where it became a waterspout for approximately five to seven minutes, meandering slowly from north to south over the water before moving back onshore in the Bay St. Lucie community around 6:20 p.m.

The strongest wind gusts occurred in the Bay St. Lucie community, where the tornado caused numerous downed trees and large branches, along with damage to well-built homes with tile roofs from winds of 65 to 75 mph. The tornado continued west into Port St. Lucie communities near the Southbend area, where it caused discontinuous damage including downed trees, blown-over fences, and damaged or destroyed pool screen enclosures before dissipating. Allison Rogers, who lives off Southbend Boulevard across from Jessica Clinton Park, said her fence was blown down during the storm.

The entire event lasted approximately 14 to 15 minutes, making it unusually long for this type of tornado. No injuries were reported from the tornado. The National Weather Service worked alongside the City of Port St. Lucie Emergency Management and St. Lucie County Emergency Management to conduct interviews with residents and piece together the timeline of the event.

hero.teaser: The National Weather Service announced late Sunday night that it will conduct a storm survey Monday morning after a tornado touched down near Jessica Clinton Park in Port St. Lucie

cards.body:
The National Weather Service confirmed an EF0 tornado with peak winds of 75 mph touched down in Port St. Lucie Sunday evening, destroying fences, sheds and pool screen enclosures in the Southbend area before dissipating. The tornado touched down at 6:10 p.m. near Southeast Kitchen Cove Lane and Southeast Morningside Boulevard, near the Tarpon Bay Club, and traveled a little more than two miles over 14 to 15 minutes. Will Ulrich, a warning coordination meteorologist with the National Weather Service, said the tornado moved over the St. Lucie River where it became a waterspout that meandered slowly for five to seven minutes before moving back onshore near the Bay St. Lucie community at about 6:20 p.m. The strongest wind gusts occurred in the Bay St. Lucie community before the circulation continued west into Port St. Lucie's Southbend area, where damage included trees down, fences blown over and pool screen enclosures damaged or destroyed. No homes were damaged and no injuries occurred.

Allison Rogers, who lives off Southbend Boulevard across from Jessica Clinton Park, said her fence was blown down and her shed was swirling around during the storm. Rogers and her roommate cleaned up the yard Monday morning and discovered nails, wood beams, furniture and lawn equipment had been moved. Rogers said she never lost power and only had cosmetic damage to the fence and shed. Rogers, who was born and raised in the area, said she had never seen anything like the storm.

The National Weather Service said it is also aware of damage reported in Jensen Beach. Based on preliminary information from Martin County Emergency Management, storm spotter calls and videos submitted to local media, forecasters said a brief landspout or tornado likely developed near the Treasure Coast Square Mall. The weather service said the possible tornado lofted a small amount of debris and caused minor damage.

The storms caused problems farther south Sunday night. In Jupiter, a large tree fell across the road near Donald Ross Road and Central Boulevard. Jupiter police responded and blocked the area to prevent drivers from hitting the tree.

A 36-year-old Fort Pierce man has been charged with manslaughter after a 34-year-old man died following a BB gun shooting on Avenue G on August 22, 2026. Jabari Cowart, 36, was charged and taken to the St. Lucie County Jail.

Fort Pierce Police officers responded to the 2900 block of Avenue G following reports of a gunshot victim. Officers located the 34-year-old male suffering from an injury. The victim was transported to Lawnwood Hospital, where he later died.

The initial investigation revealed that a group of males had been shooting a BB gun at trees when Cowart asked to use the BB gun. During the interaction, Cowart reportedly pointed the BB gun in the victim's direction and fired. Shortly thereafter, the victim collapsed. The circumstances surrounding the incident remain under investigation.

Fort Pierce will spend $31,000 in taxpayer money on an outside search firm to find a permanent city attorney after nearly the entire legal department resigned following the city's decision not to renew the current city attorney's contract. The commission approved the contract Monday during a heated special meeting, with City Commissioner Michael Broderick calling it a complete waste of taxpayer money and the situation a self-inflicted wound. Aside from one paralegal, the entire legal department has left.

Commissioner Chris Dzadovsky suggested the resignations were orchestrated, though he did not say by whom. The departures included at least three city attorneys. Broderick expressed concern that the lack of legal representation could make it easier for developers to push projects through, particularly a pending 900-unit residential project at Causeway Cove on South Hutchinson Island. Dzadovsky disagreed, arguing the absence of legal staff would actually slow development down because it would take longer to have legal review.

City Human Resources Manager Jared Sorenson defended the $31,000 contract, saying an outside firm was needed to keep the process impartial. The commission appointed Deputy City Manager Camille Wallace as interim city attorney while the permanent search is conducted. Broderick said he is not aware of any complaints, disciplinary action or poor performance reviews that would have led to the city attorney's departure.

cards.body:
The mass departure followed the city's decision not to renew the current city attorney's contract, which expires in September. City staff confirmed that aside from one paralegal, the entire legal department has left. City Commissioner Michael Broderick told WPTV the entire staff left and there are no city attorneys right now. Broderick called the situation a self-inflicted wound and said he is not aware of any complaints, disciplinary action or poor performance reviews that would lead to the attorney leaving.

Commissioner Chris Dzadovsky suggested the resignations were not spontaneous. Dzadovsky said he thinks this was orchestrated in which the members of the city attorney's office chose not to renew contracts and resign. Broderick said the departures included at least three city attorneys. Broderick expressed concern that the lack of legal representation could make it easier for developers to push projects through, particularly on South Hutchinson Island, where a 900-unit residential project is already pending at Causeway Cove.

The commission's decision to spend $31,000 on an outside search firm drew sharp criticism from both Broderick and taxpayer Kevin Keene, who spoke during public comment. Keene said this is a substantial cost now being presented after the city had advanced notice the city would become vacant and nevertheless failed to orderly execute a succession process. The commission ultimately approved the $31,000 contract and appointed Deputy City Manager Camille Wallace as interim city attorney while the permanent search is conducted.

Aaron Christiansen said he was home when he noticed something strange through his window. He said he looked across and saw dark clouds and a bunch of white. He said that looks like a lot of birds, and he got closer and realized that's not birds, that's debris. Christiansen tried to hustle his dogs into his bedroom so they could all take cover. He said they had about 10 seconds to react before the storm hit.

Christiansen found significant damage in his backyard. His patio furniture was submerged in his pool, his pool fence was blown toward his home, debris was scattered across the ground and plants were blown away. Christiansen, originally from Minnesota, said his experience with tornado-like weather helped him know what precautions to take. He and his family and pets were not injured. Christiansen said he received the emergency alert after the storm had already hit. Christiansen said he plans to begin cleanup efforts Monday and will also have his roof inspected.

hero.body:
The National Weather Service confirmed an EF0 tornado with peak winds of 75 mph touched down in Port St. Lucie Sunday evening, damaging 20 to 30 homes along a 2.1-mile path. Will Ulrich, warning coordination meteorologist with the National Weather Service Melbourne office, announced the findings Monday morning during a press conference at Jessica Clinton Park following a damage survey of the affected areas.

The tornado, classified as a landspout, first touched down at 6:10 p.m. near Southeast Kitching Cove Lane and Southeast Morningside Boulevard, close to the Tarpon Bay Yacht Club. It produced minimal structural damage, including roof damage, soffit damage and pool enclosures lifted from their foundations. The tornado then moved over the St. Lucie River, where it became a waterspout for approximately five to seven minutes, meandering slowly from north to south over the water before moving back onshore in the Bay St. Lucie community around 6:20 p.m.

The strongest wind gusts occurred in the Bay St. Lucie community, where the tornado caused numerous downed trees and large branches, along with damage to well-built homes with tile roofs from winds of 65 to 75 mph. The tornado continued west into Port St. Lucie communities near the Southbend area, where it caused discontinuous damage including downed trees, blown-over fences, and damaged or destroyed pool screen enclosures before dissipating. Allison Rogers, who lives off Southbend Boulevard across from Jessica Clinton Park, said her fence was blown down during the storm.

The entire event lasted approximately 14 to 15 minutes, making it unusually long for this type of tornado. No injuries were reported from the tornado. The National Weather Service worked alongside the City of Port St. Lucie Emergency Management and St. Lucie County Emergency Management to conduct interviews with residents and piece together the timeline of the event.

hero.body:
The National Weather Service confirmed an EF0 tornado with peak winds of 75 mph touched down in Port St. Lucie Sunday evening, destroying fences, sheds and pool screen enclosures in the Southbend area before dissipating. The tornado touched down at 6:10 p.m. near Southeast Kitchen Cove Lane and Southeast Morningside Boulevard, near the Tarpon Bay Club, and traveled a little more than two miles over 14 to 15 minutes. Will Ulrich, a warning coordination meteorologist with the National Weather Service, said the tornado moved over the St. Lucie River where it became a waterspout that meandered slowly for five to seven minutes before moving back onshore near the Bay St. Lucie community at about 6:20 p.m. The strongest wind gusts occurred in the Bay St. Lucie community before the circulation continued west into Port St. Lucie's Southbend area, where damage included trees down, fences blown over and pool screen enclosures damaged or destroyed. No homes were damaged and no injuries occurred.

Allison Rogers, who lives off Southbend Boulevard across from Jessica Clinton Park, said her fence was blown down and her shed was swirling around during the storm. Rogers and her roommate cleaned up the yard Monday morning and discovered nails, wood beams, furniture and lawn equipment had been moved. Rogers said she never lost power and only had cosmetic damage to the fence and shed. Rogers, who was born and raised in the area, said she had never seen anything like the storm.

The National Weather Service said it is also aware of damage reported in Jensen Beach. Based on preliminary information from Martin County Emergency Management, storm spotter calls and videos submitted to local media, forecasters said a brief landspout or tornado likely developed near the Treasure Coast Square Mall. The weather service said the possible tornado lofted a small amount of debris and caused minor damage.

The storms caused problems farther south Sunday night. In Jupiter, a large tree fell across the road near Donald Ross Road and Central Boulevard. Jupiter police responded and blocked the area to prevent drivers from hitting the tree.
